1. Click (16,14) → select cross
2. Click (16,26) → cross moved to (16,26)
3. Click (16,26) → select cross at (16,26)
4. Click (16,38) → cross moved to (16,38)

6. Click (16,44) → select cross at (16,44)
7. Click (16,32) → ALL crosses removed
So the pattern is: select a cross, click on an empty cell to move it there. But clicking on a cross when another cross is selected removes ALL crosses.
Wait, but in step 7, clicking on (16,32) which is a cross position, removed all crosses. So the mechanic is:
- Click on a cross when nothing is selected → select it
- Click on an empty cell when a cross is selected → move the selected cross to that cell
- Click on a cross when another cross is selected → remove ALL crosses
- Click on an empty cell when nothing is selected → select that cell
- Click on another empty cell when an empty cell is selected → ???
So to remove crosses, I need to click on a cross when another cross is selected. But that removes ALL crosses, not just one.
Actually, looking at the history again, after all crosses were removed (N=0), clicking on (57,6) reset the board (N=5). So (57,6) is a reset button.
Let me think about what the goal might be. The bottom grid has 1 cross. Maybe the goal is to have exactly 1 cross in the top grid, matching the bottom grid's pattern. Or maybe the goal is to have 0 crosses in the top grid.
Let me try a different approach. Instead of trying to remove crosses, let me try to move them to specific positions. The bottom grid has a cross at (52,44), which is in the bottom-left corner of the 2x2 grid. Maybe I need to move all top crosses to the bottom grid somehow.
